## Scope — take gap 1 ONLY. The card tells you this; I am making it binding.

The card carries three gaps and grades them itself. ⛔ They are not one job.

### ✅ IN SCOPE — gap 1, the authored-node bypass

`renderers/complex/data-table.tsx:1974` renders the `emptyAction` slot by resolving the registry **directly** — `ComponentRegistry.get(node.type)` — so the node never passes through `SchemaRenderer`, and a `visibleWhen` on it is **never evaluated**. The card calls this *"the only authored-node bypass in the tree"* and *"the actionable one"*: same declared-not-enforced class that #5401 / #5505 just closed for `record:alert`, one level down. An author writes a gate, the platform accepts it, nothing enforces it.

### ⛔ OUT — gap 2, and it is an observation

`containers.tsx:449`'s second `ExpressionEvaluator` for item-level `page:tabs` `visibleWhen`, whose `data` binds **the row** while the node-level gate binds the **data-source adapter** — *same key, opposite meanings*. The card records it at its own stated severity: **"Nobody is measurably hurt today."** ⛔ Do not fix it. ✅ If your work gives you a cheap measurement of whether anything authored actually depends on either binding, report it — that is what would move it out of observation class.

### ⛔ OUT — gap 3, and it is MINE to route, not yours to fix

`evaluateVisibilityPredicate` short-circuits on `if (!__DEV__)`, so in a production bundle a node-gate fault is **entirely silent**. The card is explicit: *"It is also a **deliberate performance short-circuit**, so the fix is a design question — what diagnostic budget production should carry — not a bug report. **Grading it as a bug would misread it.**"* ⛔ Do not touch it. **This seat is routing it to the decision box** as the design question it is.

⚠️ But carry gap 3 as *context*, because it is why gap 1 matters: the bare-string breakage measured during objectstack#11254 produced **no console line at all** — the gate stopped gating, on a real page, in total silence. That is the mechanism by which a class-1 defect ships unnoticed.

### ⛔ DO NOT "FIX" `action-bar.tsx:300`

The card warns about this by name and so do I. That is the **other** direct-registry render, and it is the **ADR-0089 action face**, which gates on `visible` inside `action-button` / `action-icon` **by design**. ⛔ It is not a bypass. A sweep for "direct registry resolution" will catch it; the sweep is wrong, not the code.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. **The card is a rebuild of objectstack#11258 through the file-at-destination channel, and its line numbers come from a different repo's checkout.** ⛔ Re-derive `data-table.tsx:1974` and `containers.tsx:449` on **your** merge-base and report the delta. ⚠️ `packages/components` moved today (#5994, #6012, #6037) — assume drift.
2. ⭐ **The positive result in the card is the design you must not break.** `visibleWhen` is enforced **once, generically**, in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — `shouldHide` tests `visibleWhen` ahead of the hoisted `visible` (since #5454), sets `_hidden`, and `if (evaluatedSchema._hidden) return null` fires **before** the registry dispatches. ✅ So the fix is to make `emptyAction` **go through that path**, not to add a second gate inside `data-table.tsx`. ⛔ A local `visibleWhen` check bolted onto the slot would be a fourth evaluator and exactly the drift gap 2 records.
3. **Verify the bypass is real before fixing it.** Mount a `data-table` whose `emptyAction` node carries a `visibleWhen` that resolves **false**, and show it renders today. If it does not — if some enclosing path already routes it through `SchemaRenderer` — ⛔ stop and report; the card's premise would have drifted.
4. ⚠️ **`emptyAction` renders in the EMPTY state**, so your fixture has to actually reach it (no rows, no loading, no error). A pin that never renders the slot is green for the wrong reason.

## Verification

Direction predicted **before** running: with the fix in, an `emptyAction` whose `visibleWhen` resolves **false** must not render; revert and show the pin goes **red**.

**Counter-probe required, both directions:** an `emptyAction` with `visibleWhen` resolving **true** must still render, and one with **no** `visibleWhen` at all must still render. Without both, "the gate is enforced" is satisfiable by never rendering the slot — which silently deletes a feature and is invisible to the positive assertion alone. ⚠️ And add the **fault** case: a predicate naming a genuinely unbound root should behave the way the central gate behaves, not some new way — measure what that is rather than choosing it.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and separately** the removed text; ⚠️ **print the landing site rather than assuming it**, and ⚠️ **assert anchor uniqueness before writing** — both traps were measured in this round (#4730, #5927). Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`; `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

Gates by name with exit codes: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name so a zero-match silent pass cannot read as green — and distinguish the **unbuilt-closure** red (`Cannot find module @object-ui/...`) from the **missing-`node_modules`** red in a fresh worktree; they need different fixes and both were hit today), root-form vitest over `packages/components/src/renderers/complex` (⚠️ vitest guard refuses `--filter` forms — use `pnpm exec vitest run <paths>` from the repo root), eslint on changed files with merge-base delta. ⚠️ Plain `eslint .` per package — ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`; it manufactures phantom errors (measured twice today).

Changeset required. Draft PR, **`Refs #5926`** (⛔ not `Fixes` — gaps 2 and 3 remain on this card). Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them) and return it.

## PM review — **ACCEPT** (gap 1)

PR #6040, head `21b6c1952`, merge-base `b0de7a85c`. Gate read at the usual mark. ⚠️ **`Refs`, not `Fixes`** — gap 2 stays an observation here and gap 3 is now **#6038** in the decision box, so this card stays open.

### The fix is the one the dispatch asked for, and I read the diff

`ComponentRegistry.get(node.type)` and its `const node: any` are **gone**, replaced by `<SchemaRenderer schema={schema.emptyAction} />`. ✅ **No `visibleWhen` test was added in `data-table.tsx`** — the slot now goes through the one generic gate rather than gaining a fourth evaluator, which was assumption 2 and the difference between fixing this and re-creating gap 2 one slot over. ✅ `containers.tsx`, `SchemaRenderer.tsx` and `action-bar.tsx:300` all untouched.

✅ And the inline comment carries the *reason* — `shouldHide` → `_hidden` → early return before registry dispatch, plus the explicit "a second check here would be a FOURTH evaluator" — so the next person cannot re-introduce the local check as an optimisation.

### The path drift is a real find, and I verified it

> `containers.tsx` now lives at `packages/components/src/renderers/**layout**/containers.tsx` … `action-bar.tsx` at `renderers/**action**/action-bar.tsx` … **Anyone sweeping by the card's paths gets "no such file" on two of three.**

Confirmed on `main`: `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-bar.tsx` and `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx`. The card said `complex/` for both. ⚠️ That is the file-at-destination rebuild channel's characteristic failure — line numbers get re-checked, **paths get trusted** — and `data-table.tsx:1974` being exact makes it worse, because one confirmed coordinate invites trusting the other two. ✅ Reporting the drift as *path, not just line* is what makes it usable by whoever takes gap 2.

### Clause-② — the second behaviour change, **ratified**

You declared a change beyond the gate: an `emptyAction` whose `type` is missing or unregistered now gets **the platform's uniform unknown-component-type report** instead of the local silent nothing. **Ratified**, on your argument: keeping the silent drop would have been a *private consumer-side tolerance*, which is the shape this repo's contract-first rule forbids — and it is not a choice you made so much as a consequence of routing to the one gate. ✅ Declaring it rather than letting it ride under "the gate now works" is the part that matters; a reviewer can see both answers changed and price them separately. `minor` on `@object-ui/components`, matching #5454 for the same class of gate going from never-gating to gating — right precedent.

### The verification

✅ **Premise verified before fixing** — a `data-table` with `data: []` (so the empty state is genuinely reached, which was assumption 4) and an `emptyAction` carrying a false `visibleWhen` **rendered**. 2 failed / 3 passed on unmodified source. ⛔ Fixing first and pinning after would have left "was it ever broken?" unanswered.

✅ **The ablation returns the exact pre-fix numbers** — 2 failed / 3 passed, same cases — and **the three counter-probes stayed green in every leg**, which is what rules out "enforced by never rendering the slot". That was the hole the dispatch named, and it is closed by measurement rather than by argument.

✅ Anchor uniqueness asserted **before** every write (`assert s.count(OLD)==1`), landing site printed with line numbers, injected and removed text grepped separately. The #4730 / #5927 lesson applied prospectively again.

✅ **Ran wider than dispatched, on your own reading of the blast radius** — nine more `data-table` consumers outside `renderers/complex`, named individually, 9 files / 76 tests green. Widening the *verification* while holding the *fence* on edits is exactly the right asymmetry.

### ⭐ The process note is the most valuable thing here, and it is new to this lane

> a SECOND trap (the eslint-baseline measurement) restored with a **repo-relative pathspec while cwd had moved into `packages/components`**, so **the trap fired but FAILED** with *"pathspec did not match any file(s) known to git"*, leaving the tree dirty. Caught by the `diff --stat` the trap itself prints.
> **"A trap's restore command must be cwd-independent; a trap that fires is not the same as a trap that restored."**

✅ This seat has been requiring `trap … EXIT INT TERM` on every ablation all day, and has been treating *the trap existing* as the guarantee. It is not. A trap that runs and fails looks identical to a trap that worked unless something checks the tree afterwards — which is precisely why the standing rule pairs the trap with `git diff HEAD --stat` empty. **You proved that pairing is load-bearing rather than ceremonial.** It goes into the seat's standing notes, and it is the fifth harness failure a dev has caught on itself and reported today rather than absorbed.

### Gap 2 — the measurement, and its honest limit

> **10** authored `visibleWhen` predicates exist in this repo in total, and **ZERO** read `data.*` in either position. The five in `examples/schema-catalog` read `record.*` and `current_user.*` only.

✅ That is the cheap measurement the dispatch asked for, and it **supports** the card's own severity rather than inflating it — gap 2 stays observation class. ✅ And the limit is stated where it belongs: *"this measures THIS repo's examples and docs, not customer deployments — evidence of no in-repo dependence, not of no dependence anywhere."* A measurement that names what it cannot see is worth more than a larger one that does not.

### Two smaller things

✅ **The sanitizer casualty flagged rather than silently repaired** — an angle-bracket span tag in the quoted assertion text was eaten on the way into the GitHub comment, so it reads *"expected to be null"*. Correct not to re-edit (a second sanitizer pass over the footer buys nothing) and correct to name it so the two copies reconcile. ⚠️ Warned about, and hit anyway — which is why the warning stays in every dispatch.

✅ **The `as any` you added by analogy and then removed.** The first draft wrote `schema.emptyAction as any` copying `empty.tsx`; you checked, `SchemaNode` is assignable with no cast, and type-check stayed green. So the fix adds **zero** `any` to a file carrying 42 — and deletes one. ✅ Not copying a neighbour's cast without testing whether it is needed is a small discipline that compounds.

### Card state

**#5926 stays open.** Gap 2 remains an observation with the measurement above attached. Gap 3 is carved out to **#6038** (decision box) — *"what diagnostic budget should production carry for a faulting `visibleWhen`"* — because the card itself grades it a design question and ⛔ grading it a bug would misread it.

## Board correction: `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`, claim released. No work was lost.

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`.

This card showed up in a stalled-claim sweep — labelled `pm:dispatched` and assigned, with **no `claude/issue-5926-*` branch on the remote**. It is **not stalled**. Gap 1 shipped as **PR #6040** (accepted above, `Refs` not `Fixes`), and the branch was deleted post-merge — which is exactly why `git ls-remote` finds nothing.

⚠️ **Correcting my own rule, because it was unsound as stated.** I have been telling this lane that a stalled claim is established *only* by `git ls-remote --heads origin 'claude/issue-<n>*'` returning empty. That guard was added because I once inferred "no branch" from "no PR" and was wrong. But an empty `ls-remote` is **equally consistent with a merged-and-deleted branch** — it is necessary, not sufficient. The correct test is: **empty `ls-remote` AND no merged PR referencing the card.** Both #5926 and #5927 would have been wrongly re-dispatched on the old rule, duplicating finished work.

### Why the label was wrong anyway

Nothing in this lane can move this card:

- **Gap 1** — done and merged (PR #6040).
- **Gap 2** (`page:tabs` item-level evaluator binding `data` to the row while the node-level gate binds the data-source adapter) — **observation class**, and the dev's measurement supports keeping it there: **10 authored `visibleWhen` predicates exist in this repo and ZERO read `data.*` in either position.** Limit stated honestly on that measurement — it covers this repo's examples and docs, not customer deployments.
- **Gap 3** (a node-gate fault is entirely silent in a production bundle, `evaluateVisibilityPredicate` short-circuiting on `if (!__DEV__)`) — carved out to **#6038** in the decision box, because the card itself grades it a **design question** — what diagnostic budget production should carry — and ⛔ grading it a bug would misread it.

So the card is open by design and waiting on a human decision (#6038), not on a dev. `pm:blocked` is the honest state; `pm:dispatched` was telling other agents a slot was occupied that is not.

⛔ Do **not** re-dispatch this card. Gap 2 needs no fix, and gap 3 is #6038's.
